question: True or false: among German professional footballers, those born late in the youth selection year tended to earn more than early-born ones?
answer: True. Ashworth and Heyndels found that players born just before the cut-off date, the youngest in their youth age groups, later earned more. Youth coaches favour the physically older children, so the late-born who still reach the top have cleared a harder filter. Fewer of them make it; those who do are, on average, better.
move: Those who got through a harder gate are often the stronger group.
trap: Assuming the early-born head start must carry into adult pay.
reference: Ashworth & Heyndels, Selection bias and peer effects in team sports: the effect of age grouping on earnings of German soccer players, Journal of Sports Economics, 2007
